You are judging the style gate for GitHub issue #143 of the stylized-character-assets milestone in the repo at /Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs (a C++ raylib game). The new character art direction: Quaternius CC0 low-poly mesh characters assembled from modular parts, banded cel shading composed with distance fog, black inverted-hull outlines, flat texture face decals (no realistic features), on a low-poly pastel city.

Evidence screenshots (already captured, all 2560x1440) in docs/qa/screenshots/stylized/:
- 143_three_consumers.png — ONE frame with all three consumer surfaces: LEFT figure = created character (creator-preview draw path), RIGHT figure = roaming NPC (walking, happy mood on its face decal), BOTTOM-RIGHT = player avatar's first-person arm (pistol viewmodel at rest). Note both random looks happened to pick witch hats — judge material/lighting consistency, not variety (variety evidence is in the other shots).
- 139_family.png — four assembled mesh characters beside one legacy "core" blob character (the blob is the deliberate legacy-compat path, not a defect).
- 140_faces.png — one character cycling five face-pick/mood combos.
- 142_anim.png — rest stance + two walk phases + a mixed witch-head-on-soldier-body walker.
- 141_plaza.png and 142_plaza_anim.png — in-game plaza (note: a teal blob NPC with a floating emote appears there; it is a stored legacy player-created character, intentionally still rendering with the old style).
- 138_rigged_day.png / 138_rigged_night.png — the five rigged KayKit multiplayer-fallback characters under the same cel+outline treatment, noon vs 8pm.

You may also launch the game yourself for more angles if needed (from the repo root):
  caffeinate -u -t 3 && ./build/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs --frames 120 shot.png --camera 4 -8 333 --hour 12
(the PNG lands in the repo root CWD; camera args are x z yawDeg; --hour sets time of day).

Judge TWO criteria and give an explicit PASS/FAIL verdict for each, with specifics:
1. STYLE CONSISTENCY across the three consumer surfaces (created character, roaming NPC, player avatar arm): same lighting treatment (banded cel), same outline treatment, same era/fidelity of assets — nothing looks pasted in from a different game.
2. NO-UNCANNY: no realism islands (photoreal eyes/skin on stylized bodies), no broken/misplaced features that read as disturbing, no wrong-scale attachments. Stylistic simplicity is fine; creepiness is not. Note the known accepted limitation: at very steep viewing angles the flat face decal can partially hide — judge whether at NORMAL viewing angles faces read correctly.

Also list any observations short of a gate failure (nice-to-fix polish items).

Return: verdict per criterion (PASS/FAIL + one-paragraph justification each), then a bullet list of observations. This is the acceptance gate — be honest; a FAIL with specifics is more valuable than a soft pass.

content.text:
## Verdict

**Criterion 1 — Style Consistency across the three consumer surfaces: FAIL**

The created character (left, in `143_three_consumers.png`) and the roaming NPC (right, same frame) match each other closely — same cel-banded skin/cloth tones, same thin near-black inverted-hull outline visible against the sky (confirmed by pixel sampling: outline pixels ≈ RGB(32,30,38) bordering the witch-hat silhouette). But the **player avatar's first-person arm/pistol viewmodel (bottom-right of the same frame) does not carry either treatment**: pixel-sampling the gun barrel shows a single flat gray value (58,58,61) across its entire visible length — no shading bands — and the gun-to-background edge transitions directly from gray to tan with zero dark border pixels, i.e. no outline pass at all. It reads as a plain flat-shaded prop pasted in front of the cel-shaded world, which is exactly the "pasted in from a different game" failure mode the criterion calls out.

Tracing the code: `src/app/RaylibRenderer.cpp`'s third-person character draw path (~lines 740–822) does an explicit two-pass draw per part — an inflated near-black `outlineColors` rim pass through `drawPartRecipe`/`outlineMaterial`, then the normal-color pass. The first-person arm function (~lines 905–937, `RaylibRenderer::drawViewmodel`-equivalent) only wraps its `DrawCube`/`DrawCylinderEx`/`DrawSphere` calls in `beginCharacterShader()`/`endCharacterShader()` — a single pass, no rim/outline draw. So the viewmodel picks up the cel *shader binding* but not the outline geometry pass, and because the shapes are large flat primitive faces, the banding that does apply isn't visible. This is a concrete, fixable gap, not a subjective read.
